title: Trace fanout and safe feed fallbacks
description: Select a publication or serving scenario. Each route shows where freshness, write amplification, and final policy checks are owned when the normal path is healthy or degraded.

nodes.label: Author publishes
nodes.detail: Creates a versioned post event. Publication does not itself mean every viewer is eligible to see the post.

nodes.label: Fanout workers
nodes.detail: Precompute ordinary follower inbox references from durable events. They are bounded and backpressured to prevent hot-author write storms.

nodes.label: Candidate store
nodes.detail: Holds recent, versioned candidate references. It improves read latency but cannot replace current policy checks.

nodes.label: Viewer opens feed
nodes.detail: Requests a short, ordered slate with session context. The viewer should receive a decision within the serving deadline.

nodes.label: Read-time retrieval
nodes.detail: Combines candidate-store state, follow relationships, high-fanout authors, and recommendation pools when a precomputed path is incomplete.

nodes.label: Ranker and features
nodes.detail: Scores a small candidate set with session and content features. It may degrade without allowing unvalidated items to be released.

nodes.label: Final slate policy
nodes.detail: Rechecks privacy, safety, blocks, removals, repetition, creator caps, and current policy before returning a slate.

nodes.label: Eligible feed response
nodes.detail: Returns an ordered, explainable slate and emits exposure events asynchronously. It never emits an item only because it has a high stale score.

scenarios.label: Ordinary author publication
scenarios.summary: A normal author publishes. Fanout workers asynchronously prepare follower references, so later feed reads can recall the update without synchronously writing every decision at read time.
scenarios.result: The write path is durable and backpressured. Candidate references improve recall, but the post is still checked again when a particular viewer receives a slate.

scenarios.label: Fresh personalized read
scenarios.summary: A viewer requests a feed. Read-time retrieval combines prepared and fresh sources, the ranker scores the short list, and final slate policy enforces the current rules before responding.
scenarios.result: This is the highest-personalization path. Its capacity must be protected by candidate reuse, deadlines, and independent fallback sources.

scenarios.label: Hot author fanout backlog
scenarios.summary: A high-fanout author creates more follower writes than the fanout workers should accept at once. The system avoids a write storm and retrieves the author on read for suitable viewers instead.
scenarios.result: Hybrid fanout trades some freshness and extra read work for controlled write amplification. The system must expose the backlog and freshness cost rather than silently dropping the post.

scenarios.label: Ranker deadline exceeded
scenarios.summary: The heavy ranker misses its deadline. Retrieval supplies a bounded-age candidate batch, and the final policy gate still filters it for current restrictions and session repetition.
scenarios.result: Personalization quality may fall, but the response remains within the deadline and stale candidates do not bypass privacy, safety, or slate constraints.

scenarios.label: Policy uncertainty on a candidate
scenarios.summary: A post has a pending restriction or uncertain safety evidence. Retrieval and ranking can complete, but final policy removes the item rather than treating a cached score as permission to show it.
scenarios.result: The feed selects another eligible candidate or returns fewer items. Failing closed on the affected item preserves the invariant even when the rest of the serving path is healthy.
